correctness.rationale: From the precise Jevtić–Živaljević definition, a generator is k successive cyclic partial sums for one length 2 and k−1 lengths 1, total circumference n=k+1. Each proper prefix sum is strictly increasing in an integer lift and less than n, so each facet has exactly k of the n vertices; hence it is a simplex-boundary facet. Choosing the 2 last gives {x,x+1,...,x+k−1}, missing x−1, and varying x achieves every missing vertex: exact equality of complexes with ∂Δ^k and homeomorphism to S^(k−1) for every k≥4. Independent enumeration of all k placements of 2 and all n starting vertices for k=4..8 gave exactly k+1 facets; symbolic argument covers every k.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge new higher-dimensional family, not the older k=3 special case. Jevtić–Živaljević arXiv:2002.09184 defines the general complex and proves a torus under genericity; repeated unit lengths violate its genericity hypothesis. Catanzaro arXiv:1612.03519 Theorem 24 identifies the triadic C(1,1,2) tetrahedral boundary, but its triadic classification does not give k≥4 in this different arbitrary-k construction. A published all-distinct nongeneric four-length Tonnetz has wedge homotopy, not this simplex boundary. No literal prior all-k family was found in named parameter, equivalent simplex-boundary, repeated-length, and sphere searches.
